[[sn:Caspia, Goddess of the Caspian Sea]][[sn:Caspia, Goddess of the Caspian Sea]]{{nymphs}}
Caspia, the Goddess of the Caspian Sea, is a divine figure revered by the people living in the region surrounding the Caspian Sea, which is the largest enclosed inland body of water in the world. Caspia is believed to be the guardian and protector of the Caspian Sea, a majestic and awe-inspiring deity who commands the winds, waves, and creatures of the sea.

As the Goddess of the Caspian Sea, Caspia is often depicted as a beautiful and regal figure, adorned with pearls and seashells, and crowned with a tiara made of waves. She is said to have the power to calm or stir the waters of the sea, depending on her mood, and her benevolence is sought by fishermen, sailors, and those who depend on the sea for their livelihood.

Caspia is also believed to have a deep connection with the surrounding lands, influencing the climate, fertility, and prosperity of the region. She is often associated with abundance, fertility, and the cycle of life, and is honored with offerings, rituals, and prayers by those who seek her favor.

As a deity of the Caspian Sea, Caspia is revered as a powerful and mystical force, embodying the majesty and mystery of the sea, and commanding the respect and awe of those who dwell near its shores. Her name is spoken with reverence, and her blessings are sought by those who venture onto the waters of the Caspian Sea, recognizing her as the divine guardian and protector of this magnificent body of water.
